# Decision Ledger

Append-only. One entry per creative decision, quoting Jeff's actual words. Entries were
captured 2026-07-05 from the exploratory Gemini session
(`sources/gemini-session-2026-07.md`, D-0001–D-0072) and its continuation
(`sources/gemini-session-2026-07-b.md`, D-0073 onward); `date` records the capture, not
the original utterance. Statuses: `ratified` (explicit), `provisional` (direction approved, substance
AI-authored), `rejected` (explicit no — kept as guardrail). Proposed material carries no
ledger entry by definition.

## D-0001 — Medium: audio-first, high-production narrative podcast
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[audio-design#Full cast, real foley]], [[overview#What this is]]
- quote: "I'm thinking a high production/audiobook like podcast."

But likely with some of these Christian invading pressures on the british isles natives with that cultural conflict."

## D-0027 — Hard magic akin to hard SF; growth-of-human-ability; the triple contrast
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[influences#Dune]], [[magic-system#Hard-magic discipline, hard-SF spirit]]
- quote: "i tend to be interested in more 'growth of human ability' type of systems (e.g. as in Dune) but i prefer a sense of true hard magic that is spiritually related to hard SF. … i want to contrast the rules of the world, the 'stuff' that humans make, and the ways in which humans have unbounded growth potential that can be unlocked through deep application."

- status: ratified

- affects: [[naming#Diegetic vocabulary discipline]], [[tone-style#The allegory discipline]], [[allegory#The discipline]], [[overview#The allegory and its discipline]], [[the-empire#The modern mirrors (authors'-room only)]], [[megaliths-and-leys#Surface discipline]]

## D-0032 — Working method: the 4-axis review (plot, setting, character, conflict)
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[overview#The four axes at a glance]], [[overview#Status of this corpus]]

## D-0033 — Antagonists are systemic: incentives, the disease of greed, shades of gray
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[opposing-factions#Design note]], [[secondary-archetypes#Design rules]], [[the-empire#What the antagonist is]]
- quote: "let's also be sure to show that everyone lives within a system. bad people are bad people due to incentives. there is no idiosyncratic demon king in this story. it's the disease of greed that leads to this global sickness. and there should be a wide range of shades of gray in the world. e.g. people must be doing bad things to avoid starving. it's not a full grimdark vibe, but the setting is a bad bad place that pulls people to do bad things."

## D-0034 — Working-class complicity is a core conflict element
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[secondary-archetypes#Design rules]]
- quote: "this connects with the working class complicity intent."

## D-0035 — Telling: audio series first; fully voiced cast with foley; narrator likely omniscient
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[narrator#Role]], [[audio-design#Full cast, real foley]], [[narrator-framing#The frame]]
- quote: "this is going to be told as an audio series first, i think. dunno if it all should be from the perspective of the apprentice . certainly not all in their voice. probably an omniscient narrator. But then fully voiced for all characters with foley."

## D-0036 — Narrator owns cold open and outro; centuries-out; obliquely hopeful
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[narrator#Role]], [[narrator-framing#The frame]], [[narrator-framing#Outros]], [[narrator-framing#Mid-episode discipline]]
- quote: "yeah, maybe the narrator owns the cold open and the outro with only bits in between as needed. gives more of a centuries out perspective. can bring in song or poetry or tapestries or history quotes, very oblique sense that there is a better future after this story but not quite explicit about what happens in the world of the narrator's present (which is far removed from the story)."

## D-0037 — Cold open is a koan/fable microcosm — a tone promise (Dune-epigraph flavor)
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[narrator-framing#Cold opens]], [[influences#Dune]]
- quote: "the cold open needs to be a sort of tone promise of what's to come or some sort of taoist/zen type koan like micro cosm (maybe like the quotes in the dune chapter openings). or just the arc of the story in the episode in miniature in a sort of fable/fairy tale/legend like setting."

## D-0038 — Manuscript-at-a-remove framing (Handmaid's Tale / LOTR)
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[narrator#The manuscript at a remove]], [[narrator-framing#The frame]], [[influences#The manuscript at a remove]]
- quote: "some sense of pulling a trick from the handmaid's tale (or to a lesser extent lord of the rings) where this manuscript is drawn from a knowledge far removed in time from the events of interest."

## D-0039 — Clear musical punctuation and mood/tone motifs
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[audio-design#Music as punctuation and mood]]
- quote: "i will have some very clear musical choices that are used for punctuation (beginning and end) as well as mood/tone within the episode (e.g. danger, rising tension, excitement, romance, etc.)"

## D-0040 — Cyclical deep history: lost prosperity, hidden knowledge, human agency
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[hound#It exists and it counts]], [[cycles#The wheel of bloom and rot]], [[cycles#Hidden knowledge, staged revelation]], [[cycles#Agency turns the wheel]], [[overview#The story in one breath]], [[animals#The party's companion exists]]
- quote: "the world had more tech and prosperity in the past and lost it. it goes through cycles. sometimes growing and innovating sustainably. sometimes not. this isnt widely known but discovered by the protagonist. understood by the narrator future scholar but not told bluntly. just dripped out as a reveal about the many possible rhythms humanity can go through some cycles of good times and others of bad times with individual human agency (by our central party the three plus the wolf spirit thing) as the key example."

## D-0041 — Trauma cycles echo at individual and societal levels
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[cycles#Trauma runs in fractals]]
- quote: "needs echoes across human stories. e.g. cycles of trauma at the individual and societal level."

## D-0042 — Embodied knowledge and dying crafts vs. centralized standardization
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[economy#The grounded baseline]], [[economy#Standardization against craft]], [[artifacts-and-memory#The time-blurred inventory]], [[artifacts-and-memory#Craft as embodied memory]]
- quote: "an emphasis on human embodied knowledge. Lost crafts or crafts in danger of dying out. this is part of the mixed time period of technological specification. to a modern human, their tech is ragged. they have tarot cards but not common books (albeit rare and expensive examples of both). they have some real concept of medicine but not electricity or gas power. etc. there should be a sense of preserving and rediscovering these dying heritage, human scale crafts in the world but also the constant pressure of the upper class imposed system of centralized standardization. e.g. a sort of amazon/mass cheap crap sort of metaphor in medieval clothes."

## D-0043 — Art project: fundability ignored; listeners and production process govern format
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[episode-format#What is fixed]], [[overview#What this is]]
- quote: "i don't care about fundability. we're not that economically oriented. this is a nearly free art project just to create. ignore fundability. i can drop the initial with 4 episodes or 40. whatever. it's what works for listeners and my production process that matters."

## D-0044 — Fractal Kishōtenketsu: episode level first, then arc, act, character-range
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[episode-format#What is fixed]], [[structure#Fractal Kishōtenketsu]]
- quote: "with listener needs being tantamount, I think that we may need to do Kishōtenketsu more at an episode level to start before a listener will trust us to do it across multi episode arcs. probably needs several hierarchical levels for different aspects of the story: the episode story, the multi episode arc, the larger act arc, the full range arc of the key character, etc."

## D-0045 — Cold opens are narrator-quoted, abstract, poetic, at clear historical remove
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[narrator#The manuscript at a remove]], [[narrator-framing#Cold opens]], [[in-world-texts#The Fable of the Iron and the Thread]], [[in-world-texts#The Apocrypha of the Eaten Word]]
- quote: "id challenge us to begin our cold open from the narrator to include its own sort of zen koan like nearly impenetrable Kishōtenketsu beats at first. just pure microcosm, stated abstractly, poetically. not necessarily always literal poetry. maybe sometimes just history or apochral legends or whatever. with the clear historical remove that the narrator is quoting."

## D-0046 — REJECTED: modern-technological vocabulary in diegetic text
- status: rejected
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[naming#Diegetic vocabulary discipline]], [[tone-style#The allegory discipline]], [[in-world-texts#The Apocrypha of the Eaten Word]]
- quote: "I question the use of the word machine in example 2. risks going too far forward in technology time than we want our overall vibe to be." (Generalized per D-0030: the banned-vocabulary list in `data/banned-vocabulary.yaml` operationalizes this.)

## D-0047 — Narrator is a religious scholar of the study of Wyrd and Frith
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[narrator#Role]], [[influences#Dune]], [[religion#The requirement]], [[religion#The narrator's orders]]
- quote: "i think the narrator must be a sort of religious scholar of the history of the study of the wyrd and frith. i think there needs to be a sense of generations of religious organizations that have a deep understanding of the world. again, nods a bit to dune in flavor but grounded within the values of this specific world."

- status: ratified

- status: ratified

- status: ratified

- date: 2026-07-05

- status: rejected
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[structure#What structure is not]]
- quote: "I also don't want to have a highly tolkien esque epic fantasy quest. Seems like there needs to be more novelty in the plot bones that are less of the classic (intrinsically male) frietag's pyramid style structure."

## D-0053 — Radical humanism is the protagonist's opposing stance
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[protagonist#Radical humanism]], [[overview#The story in one breath]]
- quote: "remember that there is a radical humanism to the protagonists values. Growing people and communities is their opposing stance."

## D-0054 — Keep the Gen-Z/alpha-proxy apprentice as viewpoint character
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[apprentice#Viewpoint and entry]]
- quote: "For characters, we'll still want that gen z/alpha proxy as an apprentice/viewpoint character of some sort."

## D-0055 — Kishōtenketsu plot structure with hub-and-spoke movement through complex geography
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[regions#Principles]], [[structure#Fractal Kishōtenketsu]], [[structure#Hub and spoke]], [[anomalies#Resolution without elimination]]
- quote: "Grabbing one thread: let's flesh out a plot structure around Kishōtenketsu with the hub and spoke movement through a complex geography."

## D-0056 — Pre-history carries allegory-framed "big ideas" with major consequences
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[pre-history#Why it exists]], [[pre-history#What was lost, what remains]], [[structure#Pre-history and exploration are threaded, not front-loaded]]
- quote: "For pre history, i think we should have some big ideas (leaning on our allegory to frame it up) in the pre history. There should be major consequences to the world before that help us deeply understand what's changed what's been lost and what limited possibilities remain for the future."

## D-0057 — Diversity by circumstance, class, education, values — not modern DEI categories
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[human-variance#The requirement]], [[human-variance#Why it matters either way]]
- quote: "They need some real diversity in perspectives. But we're not doing modern dei type identities. We want to define them by circumstances, background, economic position, educational opportunities, values not skill color, sexual orientation, etc."

## D-0058 — No literal fantasy races; human variance must be made comprehensible
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[human-variance#The requirement]]
- quote: "it's unclear to me if everyone in this world is 100% human as we know it beyond great mental capacity. Worth fleshing out how humans can vary in this world. E.g. not literal dwarves, elves, wizards, orcs, etc. but we need a sense of how there are different types of people in this world. And how that is made comprehensible to the reader." (Note his explicit reservation: "Not sure we're doing monster proxies.")

## D-0059 — The ecology/environment is a "character": regions with distinct rules to discover
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[regions#Principles]], [[anomalies#Taxonomy and forensics]]
- quote: "Certainly the ecology/environment is some sort of 'character' in that they have distinct differences that vary based on backstory and separation from other regions with unique distinctive characteristics with some magical power differences that give the characters things to learn and discover."

## D-0060 — Protagonist: born outside the empire, adopted in — the Moses story
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[protagonist#The Moses arc]]
- quote: "i think the protagonist needs to be born outside of the empire and adopted in. A foot in both worlds. Rebelling is a return to a deeper identity and a rejection of a less valid upper class value system. Basically the Moses story."

## D-0061 — A plot reason is required for the apprentice's adoption
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[apprentice]], [[protagonist]], [[structure]]
- quote: "Also needs a plot reason for the apprentice to get adopted by the protagonist."

## D-0062 — Story begins with the apprentice; protagonist meets apprentice before the anchor
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[apprentice#Viewpoint and entry]], [[structure#The opening]]
- quote: "i think the protagonist needs to meet the apprentice before bringing in the anchor. Protagonist and anchor need to have back story. But the story begins with the apprentice. She is our viewpoint character (whether literally or more of as a rule of thumb for information available to the reader/listener)."

## D-0063 — Pseudo-family core group; no romance between anchor and protagonist
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[anchor#The ratified shape]]
- quote: "I think this core group is a pseudo family. E.g. there is no romance between anchor and protagonist. But sometimes they have to pretend to pass in some toxic societies they have to function in. Pretending apprentice is their daughter. Unclear if anchor is gay or just old and uninterested in sex. Certainly not romantically interested in protagonist."

## D-0064 — Animal elements in the party (dog/wolf-spirit question opened)
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[hound#It exists and it counts]], [[animals#Animals belong in the story]]
- quote: "Might be worth adding more explicit animal elements as well. E.g. does the apprentice get a dog? Are there dogs like our dogs or more magical wolves with the free choice to work with humans." (Nature of the companion remains Q-0006; D-0040 later says "the three plus the wolf spirit thing".)

## D-0065 — Protagonist personality: calm supreme competence with a quirky-childish tension
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[protagonist#Personality and voice]]
- quote: "I really love the mix of supreme maturity and depth of competence balanced with quirky childishness of freiren. I dont want to take that literally but i need some sense of the core tension in the character. And i also need to like them aesthetically enough to spend a huge amount of time with them. E.g. i don't like some of the shouty tropes of anime and they will get more tiring in this long form audio drama. Consider how the character can be both very calm and controlled while still compelling and with variation over a longer plot."

## D-0066 — Apprentice: period-appropriate non-binary, pre-adolescent, trauma-real, not hot-headed
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[apprentice#Identity]]
- superseded-by: D-0219
- quote: "I do think that we should define the apprentice as a period appropriate version of non-binary. Their age is pre sexual maturity at the start and they dont get treated consistently as male or female by their pseudo parents and the plot may require them to dress or behave one way or the other. … with gender not being the apprentices chief concern but rather other driving plot elements. They need a real backstory. E.g. how do they get orphaned and what does that trauma incline them towards. … And how does that avoid the tedium of the hot headed aggressive anime protagonist that gets so fucking dull."
- note: D-0219 supersedes only the gender-identity portion. The age, agency, trauma discipline, and rejection of the hot-headed adolescent trope remain binding.

## D-0082 — The line-by-line register: adult, sincere, humanistic; no stagey anime writing
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-05
- affects: [[tone-style#Adult register]], [[influences#Line-by-line touchstones]], [[overview#What this is]]
- quote: "we want touchstone authors (from a range of media types) to guide the authorship of not just plot but also narration, dialogue, and characterization. i like the eastern influences of the plot structure and the zen koan like parables. but i want to avoid very immature, stagey anime style writing aimed at teens. this piece isn't GoT style trauma exploitation but it's dark enough to be pitched at adults. and i want this sense of there being real wisdom and perspective in the narrator but plausibility in the characters the protagonist should be clearly a different sort of not quite human thing due to the accumulation of knowledge and personalities. but the whole thing should have a tone that serves its ultimately pro humanistic narrative that works for what is ultimately some new flavor of fantasy adventure. it should feel natural to weave in songs and poetry and scraps of ancient history. yet characters should sound in their dialogue utterly real and human."

## D-0107 — Title round-1 verdicts: tone/thesis first, neutral-to-optimistic, religious register
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-06
- affects: [[naming]], [[overview]], [[narrator-framing]]
- quote: "series naming isn't there yet. needs to speak to the overall tone/thesis of the piece. e.g. The Wyrd Way is probably almost typeoutable with a bit of autocorrect to do weird to wyrd. and way grounds it in a journey and a way of being. there is a strong religious tone to the narrators perpsective. i want to speak to the neutral to optimistic parts of the piece, not the grim parts. shit like salt and rust are really cliched in fantasy. the [odd adjective][odd noun] pattern isn't bad, but it needs more options to really get to something good. frithward isn't bad but isn't a winner either. work this one some more with these different perspectives and come up with a new crop of candidates."
- note: Verdicts — "Salt and Rust" dead (fantasy cliché); "Frithward" alive but not a winner; "The Wyrd Way" a promising direction (autocorrect/search-forgiveness softens the wyrd-spelling objection; "way" grounds journey + way-of-being, echoing the koan/Tao strand); titles must speak to tone/thesis, may carry the narrator's religious tone, and must lean neutral-to-optimistic, never grim; the [odd adjective][odd noun] pattern is viable but needs volume to find a good one.

## D-0108 — Batch-002 verdicts: name structures, doublespeak framework, first ratified places
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-06
- affects: [[regions#The ratified names]], [[naming#Round-two calibration (batch-002 verdicts)]]
- quote: "batch 2 names: audrey hits the tiffany problem. no. needs to more clearly signal the genre. should be clearly feminine. not obviously grandmotherly like edit or hilda. all stans sound male. wynne is too unclear in audio. also the protagonist needs a given and family name (which probably don't match). she's a bastard child half of one society and half of another. should be in the name. for apprentice aalto is fine but still no matching additional name. presumably aalto is the family name but also what people call them. for anchor, needs more work but i like ketilson as the family name. just needs to explore more broadly for given names. for the wolf spirit, i'm fine with wed, or maybe ward as the suffix, but you need to explore more broadly on prefixes. really a bunch of bad directions on the narrators name. for the imperial framework, it nees more orwellian double speak. e.g. the gift, the balance, etc. the narrator's order ideas (like some others) are going off in a direction of violence and maleness that this series stands opposed to. really not tracking well. for salt fringes halspetra will do. starting spoke should switch to Gwern. and yes, trefpen is approved. update accordingly."
- note: Rejections — Audrey (Tiffany problem: authentic-but-reads-modern), Edith/Hilda (grandmotherly), -stan forms (read male), Wynne (audio-unclear), the narrator-name directions (third strike), the order names (read violent/male — against the series' core, D-0005). Approvals — Aalto = apprentice family name AND common address (given name still needed); Ketilson = anchor family name (given names to explore); hound suffix wed (or ward), prefixes to explore; Halspetra = salt-fringes region ("will do"); GWERN = the starting-spoke valley (switches from the D-0102 Ffynnonhen lean — noted, not a formal supersession since D-0102's ff-/ll- calibration stands); TREFPEN = the hub, approved outright. New directions — imperial framework needs Orwellian doublespeak (the Gift, the Balance: benevolent words for extraction); protagonist name must signal genre and be clearly feminine.

## D-0118 — Q-0008 resolved: variance is circumstance-not-species; liminality is debt-written; the Archive is a fourth variance

- note: Confirms the triad — sheltered ("chalk-blooded"), spent ("bog-touched"), Wyrd-marked ("liminal") — but frames all three as circumstance written on the body, never species (D-0058); adds the protagonist's Archive-condition as a fourth variance (great cognition is something the Tithe DID to a body, with costs). Core mechanic of liminality = debt-written: axiomatic debt writes a person the way it sours a spring (a spectrum, reversible early, fixed late), read on the same gauge as soil, beast, and spirit — which is what keeps liminals out of "monster proxy" territory (D-0105). Variants: heritable lineages (generations at fouled edges) and treaty-touched (the honoured cost of deep treaty with a landvættir). Social position varies by who reads them (empire = witchery or tool; natives = sacred or kin). Labels stay working descriptors, not proper names (Q-0002). Resolves Q-0008.

## D-0119 — Q-0009 resolved: four biome-nations, core-and-ring over a downstream watershed; sketches become anomaly deep-zones

- note: The map is four biome-nations in a core-and-ring arrangement — the chalk core (Whitecombe) high in the middle, the lowlands (Corsbach), crags (Swartby), and salt fringes (Halspetra) around it, coast outermost, all ringed by permanent storm-wrack. The first hub is the lowlands valley Gwern/Trefpen; the party migrates outward and the arc ends at the chalk core — Moses returning to where she began (this encodes the macro-arc: sabotage the periphery, then breach the core). Underlying hydrology is downstream: extraction flows crags → lowlands → fringes, debt made visible as water. Each biome-nation may hold 2–3 sub-nations for a multi-hundred-episode run (D-0051); finer adjacency and the other hubs are drawn as spokes are written. The earlier sketches (Glass Weald, the memory-eating valley, Rust Wastes) are reabsorbed as anomaly deep-zones inside the biomes, not separate nations. Names per D-0101/D-0108/D-0111. Resolves Q-0009.

## D-0125 — Bonus adopted: the six anomaly manifestation modes; the embodied creature is the rare earned endpoint
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-06
- affects: [[anomalies#The manifestation modes]]
- quote: "all of the suggestions in the open questions are approved as suggested. not all perfect, but well motivated. just need some passes through ai tic detection and adaptation downstream. but nothing more from me. get them in"
- note: Adopts the manifestation-modes ladder requested alongside Q-0008 and blessed by the omnibus. Six modes, subtle-to-embodied: (1) seasonal/weather wrongness, (2) behavioural corruption (beasts, then people), (3) pattern-wrongness and absence, (4) slow material rot, (5) spatial/temporal seams, and (6) — rarely — an embodied creature. A single trouble usually escalates through several modes as its debt accumulates; keeping the creature last and rare is what stops the show becoming monster-of-the-week (D-0012). Audio-first: each mode carries its own sound treatment. Liminal people (D-0118) are the human reading on the same gauge. Promoted into [[anomalies]] as a ratified section citing (D-0105, D-0125). Extends D-0105.

## D-0128 — Craft doctrine: stored knowledge + enforcement tooling for good writing
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-06
- affects: [[craft-pillars#Aesthetic sobriety]], [[craft-pillars#Rhizomatic restoration]], [[craft-pillars#Material sovereignty]], [[craft-pillars#Earnest sincerity]]
- quote: "now, spawn another agent to build out stored knowledge and code tools to enforce what is good writing. it should begin with some research that fleshes out these initial kernels i'll give you on fantasy specifically as well as episodic and audio drama. these should be used in outlining, in settling character lore and setting choices. to guide generation, to check generation to point to opportunities to improve in bar raising, etc. what is good writing is a ubqituous concern and you should both take my sources, research them and expand into related guidance while also thinking about how to rigorously toolify them and prevent bad work from slipping through the cracks."
- note: The author supplied four kernels: (1) the Sanderson lecture corpus (promise/progress/payoff, the three character sliders, the laws of magic, the iceberg, window-pane prose, the pyramid of abstraction, MICE quotient, try/fail cycles, show-vs-tell nuance, said-tag discipline); (2) serialized-fiction craft (episode/season structure, open loops, world-as-plot-engine, micro-pacing, per-installment promise); (3) audio-drama craft (SFX as character, the 60-second hook, 3-4 voices per scene, vocal signatures, strategic name-pepper, the power of silence, read-aloud discipline, no as-you-know-Bob); (4) his negative-mold manifesto, filed as the four craft pillars in [[craft-pillars]]. Standing rule: where generic craft advice conflicts with the pillars or existing canon (e.g. escalation-is-everything vs. the meditative register; err-on-awesome vs. sobriety), THE PILLARS WIN — the knowledge base must record such tensions explicitly with the mission-side resolution.

- quote: "title is better but needs some (ideally subtle) relationship to the humanistic values of the piece. e.g. \"Bound Together,\" which could be read as a negative constraint but is actually the strength of the core party and the community. really needs some sense of starting from the values of the piece at its highest level and then connecting to the plot, character, setting. values are more locked in. all the rest is still pretty fucking wet clay. do another title round that tries to build a bit more ground up. i think there needs to be some subtle, oblique, non-obvious wordplay (at least double meaning) in whatever we pick."
- note: Round-4 method ratified: generation starts from the VALUES at their highest level (radical humanism, mutual aid, frith-as-law, maintenance, craft-dignity, found-family, consent, memory outlasting power) and connects DOWN to plot/character/setting — the reverse of round 3's material-first tether, because values are locked while the material is still wet clay. HARD REQUIREMENT: subtle, oblique, non-obvious wordplay — at least a double meaning, ideally the author's example shape ("Bound Together"): a surface reading available as negative constraint whose true reading is the community's strength. The title should perform, in miniature, the language-reclamation the resistance itself performs.

## D-0137 — Title round-4 verdict: erudite elevation + googleable uniqueness required
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-06
- affects: [[naming]], [[overview]]
- quote: "for the titling run, it's a good approach, but yielded no winners. e.g. shit like \"teller\" will resonate with bank tellers, which isn't viable. the commons isn't googleably unique, which is another requirement. all told is definitely in use as some sort of podcast or chat show or something. the list is just generally flat. it needs at least one word that elevates it to make it a bit impenetrable on first glance. likely also helps with googleability. e.g. i'm currently digging, \"Broken and Bound Together\" but i'd like something with a bit more unique and erudite diction to really reward a sort of multiple perspectives on the piece over years of story."
- note: The values-first + double-meaning method stands; the diction was too common. New hard requirements: (1) at least one ELEVATED/erudite word — slightly impenetrable on first glance; (2) googleable uniqueness — an exact-phrase search must be ownable; (3) the title must reward multiple perspectives over years of story — the meanings keep unfolding. Kills: the Teller (bank-teller resonance), the Commons (not googleably unique), All Told (in use). The author's current dig: "Broken and Bound Together" — its shape (brokenness + binding as strength) is live; the diction wants elevating.

## D-0152 — The seven craft tensions ruled, one by one (PD-4)
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-06
- affects: [[craft-pillars#The seven tensions, ruled]], [[narrator-framing#The narration registers]]
- quote: "craft tensions: 1: correct, don't escalate intensity. 2. also correct. 3. yep, correct. 4. eh, sorta not quite. i kinda agree with competence as a source of compelling listener interest. it just shouldnt necessarily showy, arrogant, or noisy (at least in enfys). 5. yeah, we'll have some tension here. there will always be movement but pure relationship deepening type plot points, richness in understanding and emotional growth count. 6. yeah, this is where to start but we'll see. narrator's quotes are one tone. most narration is windowpane. but then there are times when the narrator's register reveals future knowwledge. and how enfys does the proofs will have to be figured out. definitely needs its own register (maybe even specific language). 7. i dunno, i think we're kinda following that advice fits. it's just cycles within cycles."
- note: Tensions 1-3 (escalate understanding not intensity; the climax is the ten; wonder-amid-ruin over spectacle) ratified as written. Tension 4 AMENDED: competence IS a compelling engine and may be savored on-mic — it must simply never be showy, arrogant, or noisy IN ENFYS; the constraint is hers, not a house rule against display. Tension 5 CONFIRMED with the counting rule made explicit: there is always movement, and pure relationship-deepening, richness of understanding, and emotional growth COUNT as movement. Tension 6 PROVISIONAL as the starting point, with new doctrine: the narrator's QUOTES are one tone; most narration is WINDOWPANE; at times the narrator's register reveals FUTURE KNOWLEDGE. How Enfys performs the proofs is unresolved — it definitely needs its own register, maybe even specific language (new Q-0018). Tension 7 REFRAMED as no real conflict: the Event-thread advice fits — order does return, as a new cycle's equilibrium; cycles within cycles.

## D-0178 — Campaign-015 listener-proxy evaluation must be fresh and non-leading
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-08
- affects: []
- quote: "for the SAMPLE-SPEC questions, i think there's just a methodlogy thing about needing to ensure that new agents spawned don't get leading questions but get fresh contexts without bias and then asked reasonable questions that proxy for reader experience. then we'll have a better feel for what a listener will catch"
- quote_2: "possibly also a good use for strong listener persona prompts and/or flash/small models"
- note: Campaign-015 voice-proving evaluation must separate generation from listener-proxy evaluation. Listener-proxy agents get fresh, non-leading contexts and are not shown expected answers, target interpretations, rubrics that reveal intended comprehension, or generation prompts. Their prompts should proxy first-listen reader/listener experience with neutral questions: what they understood happened, what changed, who wanted what, what confused them, what they expect next, and whether they would continue. Strong listener-persona prompts and small/flash models may be used for broader comprehension sweeps, with a stronger model as calibration or adversarial audit. This does not authorize paid OpenRouter usage, xAI models, live voice APIs, real voice IDs, or any bypass of D-0177 constraints.

## D-0179 — No-narrator table-read packets failed; narrator must carry audio gaps
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-08
- affects: [[narrator-framing#Mid-episode discipline]], [[narrator-framing#The narration registers]], [[tone-style#The register map]]
- quote: "from the table reads: \"sickbed, tide, cord\" does not work at all. it presumes fucking magic from SFX to a ludicrous degree and from the listener. the gaps are what the narrator is there to do. solid failure. \"The Missing Weathers\" is another example of setting the floor too high for SFX and ignoring the job of the narrator. again, fail. same shit with \"The House that Would Not Dry\" looks like a broad issue"
- quote_2: "make sure you understand how truly limited SFX is as a tool. we can't have it be such a huge character. many of these things will be best effort generated sound effects, not necessarily well calibrated, well heard image painting for the lisenter. this is related to the narrator thing."
- quote_3: "this is piece is more audio book than old school radio play"
- note: The campaign-014 no-narrator table-read packets for ep01, ep07, and ep10 are invalid as positive evidence. D-0176 means the narrator must avoid direct address, host framing, and promise-selling; it does not mean absence. The medium target is closer to audiobook-with-cast/foley than old-school radio play. SFX/foley is limited, best-effort support and must not become a huge semantic character or the primary carrier of causal comprehension. The narrator has a necessary load-bearing windowpane function: orienting causality, action gaps, time, off-mic state, and object relationships that SFX/foley cannot honestly carry alone. Future table-read and voice-proving samples must test narrator-bearing revisions rather than asking listeners to infer magic from sound cues.

## D-0180 — The single proof-system architecture approved; magic pedagogy commissioned
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-09
- affects: [[magic-system#Core law]], [[magic-system#Hard-magic discipline, hard-SF spirit]], [[magic-system#Extended cognition: artifacts as mind]], [[magic-system#The cost]], [[magic-system#The chorus: distributed proof-speaking]], [[magic-system#What magic is not]], [[artifacts-and-memory#The deck]], [[artifacts-and-memory#The loom and the knot]], [[animals#Animals as co-processors]], [[the-turning#What it is]], [[the-turning#Counsel, never prophecy]], [[megaliths-and-leys#The standing circles]], [[regions#The four-biome frame]]
- quote: "ok. i read DP-002-hard-magic-dramatic-function.md . it's basically all approved. but then we need to do a bunch more extension work to play out the futher decisions needed. additionally, we need some sense of a pedagogy: how and when are we introducing which concepts. this needs some serious fucking pacing and various pedagogical strategies to ensure that people who missed stuff have paths to get back on. otherwise, people could bounce off the denseness of the piece. build this out in planning infra. needs again both code and data that makes this pedagogy of magic system something supervisable over 400ish episodes with appropriate supervision affordances. report on the rest of your status"
- note: DP-002's central architecture is approved: there is one magic, lawful proof over Wyrd-and-Frith; knots, the Turning, paper/weaves/books, standing circles, magical animals, landvaettir, and regions are interfaces for finding, holding, checking, distributing, timing, witnessing, or localizing premises, not separate magic systems. The negative boundaries also hold: music/rite, prophecy, vague intention, destiny, element powers, violence, and moral purity are not working magic. This approval does not settle every downstream design choice. It commissions substantial extension work plus durable planning infrastructure for magic-system pedagogy over the roughly 400-episode series: concept introduction order, prerequisites, repetition, recovery paths for listeners who missed details, narrator burden, density limits, and supervision affordances in code and data.

## D-0210 — The series has exactly four approximately fifty-episode acts
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-11
- affects: [[structure#Fractal Kishōtenketsu]], [[structure#The macro arc]]
- supersedes: D-0168 (episode arithmetic only), D-0208 (episode arithmetic and eight-act interpretation only)
- quote: "the spec on this is wrong, \"Repair the typed 400-episode series portfolio after D-0208: replace the obsolete four 100-episode acts with at least eight acts of no more than 50 episodes while preserving the ratified series-level sabotage, breach, and world-after movements; retain Act I as a 46-to-50 episode active planning capacity without selecting a quarantined story chassis; update synchronizer tests so stale act arithmetic fails closed and next-runnable planning stays bounded.\" the brief, again, is 4 acts. no alternatives. 200ish total episodes. only vary by 10%. roughly 50 episodes per act. only vary by 10%. no limits or minimums on arcs within acts but use an arc structure within acts. fractal japanese 4 beat thing wherever possible. you keep veering off of spec on this structural stuff. do a review and enforce more strongly across all tpth work"
- note: This is the binding series arithmetic. *To Pleach the Hedgeway* has exactly four acts, never an alternative act count. The target is approximately 200 episodes with a strict 180–220 inclusive planning range; each act targets approximately 50 episodes with a strict 45–55 inclusive range. Acts contain coherent nested arcs, but canon imposes no minimum, maximum, or fixed arc count. Fractal kishōtenketsu (ki, shō, ten, ketsu) should shape the series, acts, arcs, episodes, scenes, and smaller artifacts wherever narratively coherent; labels must not be forced where the material does not earn the shape. The four acts carry the adopted macro movement directly: sabotage across ki and shō, breach as ten, and the world after as ketsu. D-0168's approximate-400 arithmetic and D-0208's eight-act interpretation are superseded; their other ratified story, hook, clarity, and competition findings remain in force.

## D-0217 — Episode openings require sensory and seasonal grounding
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-13
- affects: [[craft-pillars#Sensory and seasonal grounding]]
- quote: "work on the openings of all episodes and build skills (deterministic and agentic) into the craft toolchain to address this general issue. quote to guide you: I'm a literary agent and one of the most common problems I see in opening pages is a lack of descriptive detail. You have the dialogue You have the inciting incident You have the characters Things happen But I don't know what the scene should look like in my head - there's nothing in my mind's eye. I don't know what the characters can hear or smell. I don't know what season it is. Adding evocative descriptive details is one of the most powerful ways you can draw in a reader, and a literary agent."
- note: Production and craft-tooling direction, not new world lore. Every episode opening must make its physical place legible, include at least one selected heard or smelled detail beyond the mere fact of dialogue, and establish weather or season. Action, dialogue, character, and inciting incident do not excuse a white-room opening. The details should act on the scene rather than becoming a room inventory. This ruling governs reusable craft briefs, generation and revision prompts, and deterministic opening checks; revision of existing script prose remains a separate production task.

## D-0218 — The narrator never describes voices or delivery
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-13
- affects: [[narrator-framing#No voice-description narration]]
- quote: "the narrator can never describe what people’s voices sound like or how they said things."
- note: This is a global narrator-register rule for every episode and script tool. Narrator records may not describe direct vocal qualities, accents or phonetics, delivery adverbs, vocal metaphors, or indirect how-said qualities attached to words, sentences, or speech. Character dialogue may mention voices. Narrator records may state neutrally that speech occurred, describe physical breathing or bodily cost, and use sound metaphors for objects, animals, weather, or nature. A fail-closed deterministic audio-script check enforces the distinction and participates in the global episode gate.

## D-0222 — TPtH uses a third-party public audio feed; Patreon waits past Arc 2

TWTH is not imminently turning on paid features. unclear that any of them are worth it for that audience. will probably just ask MoM readers to support the indie/self published book launch. record that. for the patreon trigger, i agreed that it's later in the tpth rollout. note that the rollout for tpth is faster and bigger than presumed. it's one full arc 1 as an initial release to begin. binge centric. with arc 2 coming real fast. i'm targeting the bingeiest, lore hungry of audiences first. the truly gluttons for content. and i don't need to figure out the nitty gritty of what to ask for money for on patreon to start. i think it's a later thing, deeperr into tpth, dependent on audience. no sooner than the arc 2 drop, and the ask is probably a generally support the making of tpth to hire more human artists for things like covers and voice acting, but probably state even more simploy on the site. and yeah, i need to keep the cta framed really tight and simple at each stage of growth. i'm not sure that i want to geoffrey hoxton/mom style audio podcasts on substack. generally seems like all these platforms have more than i'm likely to need. make some updates and do the little bit of  follow up work"
- note: Publication and monetization direction, not canon lore. The remaining open platform question is the TPtH web home: a plain open-web page, a page/section inside *The Way Things Hold*, or a separate Substack publication. *The Way Things Hold* is not turning on paid features imminently; paid Substack features may not fit that audience, and the near-term MoM ask is more likely support for the indie/self-published book launch than paid publication access. Patreon is later in the TPtH rollout, audience-dependent, and no sooner than the Arc 2 drop. The TPtH rollout is faster and larger than RR-019 assumed: launch begins with all of Arc 1 as a binge-centered initial release, with Arc 2 following quickly, aimed first at lore-hungry high-consumption listeners. The first Patreon ask need not name a precise production line item yet; it should probably be a very simple support-the-making-of-TPtH ask, with human artists for covers and voice acting as examples, stated plainly. CTA discipline remains binding: each stage gets one tight, simple audience action. Geoffrey Hoxton/MoM-style Substack audio podcasts remain doubtful/deferred rather than an expected stage.

- quote: "jfc. this isnt at all on voice for  the publication. what the hot fucking trash is this? the pub is about a bunch of reflective essays on how tarot helps us with our owwn searches for meaning. this is paraphrased journalism. jfc. not at all a match for what this pub does. review the stuff on the pub already and get your head on straight and write an actually viable post: https://thewaythingshold.substack.com/"
- note: Publication direction, not canon lore. The rejected **Carry the Fish Downstream** draft treated the reported occurrence as its destination and therefore failed the publication at the level of genre, regardless of factual accuracy or deterministic style scores. Rewrite it as a reflective essay in which the Brittany rescue supplies current pressure and the Six of Swords gives the question a bounded surface: what rescue, passage, and repair mean when the conditions that made a place habitable have not been restored. *The Way Things Hold* uses tarot to assist the reader's own search for meaning; it does not publish paraphrased journalism with contemplation added at the end. Future semantic review must fail closed when a draft merely summarizes reporting.

## D-0229 — Kaisla is ratified as Aalto's aunt and guardian
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-28
- affects: [[kaisla#The name and the relation]]
- quote: "Ratify Kaisla"
- note: The author selected ratification from a presented ruling offering three options — ratify Kaisla, replace her with an unnamed role, or choose a different name. The ruling is a selection, not prose; the substance is recorded here. Kaisla is now the settled proper name of Ranta Aalto's aunt and guardian, the fourth speaking role in Arc 1 Episode 1 ("The Last Dry Cord"). She is a secondary character, not core cast (D-0132). The name passes the naming oracle on all thirteen checks at secondary tier (`uv run fantasy name vet Kaisla --kind person --tier secondary --role "aunt and guardian" --gender female`), and it is register-consistent with the family it belongs to: Kaisla is the Finnic native-register given-simple form (Fi *kaisla*, "reed, rush") from the same pool as Ranta (Fi *ranta*, "shore, strand"). She entered the material through the D-0220-accepted campaign-079/080 Arc 1 development basis as Aalto's sick aunt in Episode 1. This entry ratifies the name and the aunt-and-guardian relation only. Her illness, her immobility, and the accepted design's beat in which she reaches the borrowed eave and dies of cold and prior illness remain `proposed` — D-0220's `affects:` does not name this character, so no section here may cite it. This ratification clears the tokens `Kaisla` and `Kaisla's` for the `proper-name-vetting` production gate; it does not by itself make Episode 1 acceptance-ready, because that gate still harvests `Edge` (an unratified Turning leaf name) and `Say` (from the capitalized spoken-proof response token `Say so`).

## D-0230 — Machine candidates enter as provisional and unblock work; humans ratify to close
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-28
- affects: [[in-world-texts]]
- quote: "in general, work should flow without human approval. so, machine generated candidates properly filed for a ruling can be granted a provisional state and used to unblock dependency graphs of jobs. this holds for  names, epigram sources, etc. various parts of lore. then a human mmust still ratify for it to bee closed out. just draw a reasonable line at things that overly spendy in time or credits (e.g. large generation of audio) that will require resolving all provisional to ratified. as is, the appp keeps defaulting to sitting on its hands"
- note: Process discipline, not lore content. This supersedes the standing rule that new lore enters only as `proposed` and that promotion to `provisional` is always the author's explicit act. A machine-generated lore candidate — a name, an in-world text usable as an epigraph source, or a comparable bounded artifact — MAY be admitted directly as `provisional` and cite this decision, on one condition that is not optional: it must first be filed as a live ruling-request under `docs/rulings/` so it appears in `docs/REVIEW.md` and the author can rule on it. Filed-then-provisional is the permitted path; provisional without a filed request is not. Because `provisional` is inside the generation eligibility set (`ratified` + `provisional`, `src/fantasy/canon/pack.py:24`), this releases dependent jobs immediately instead of parking a whole dependency graph behind a human. Ratification remains the author's sole act and is what closes the item; a provisional candidate the author later rejects is registered as killed, never deleted, per the standing guardrail-corpus rule. The line the author drew: work whose cost is large in time or credits — the named example is large audio generation — must NOT proceed on provisional material, and requires every provisional input it depends on to be ratified first. Cheap, reversible, provenance-preserving generation proceeds; expensive or externally-effecting work waits for the human. The defect this corrects is the application defaulting to sitting on its hands: an effects-denied posture applied to routine creative throughput, which is the same disease as a product surface whose copy states it performs no action.

## D-0234 — Episode acceptance is final; recommission instead of reopening
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-28
- affects: []
- quote: "yeah, it's not a problem for acceptance to be final. i can just recommission as needed."
- note: Resolves RQ-030. Accepting an episode stays terminal: there is no reopen, and no path to redraft work built on an accepted predecessor. When an accepted episode turns out to be wrong, the author abandons the arc and recommissions, which is what has happened every time and which works today at provider cost. This ruling closes a question that fell out of a half-built feature rather than a decision — `generation` is hardcoded to `1` at both lineage-binding branches and a second lineage per episode number is refused as `:accepted_predecessor_ambiguous`, so the `script_superseded` to `predecessor_invalidated` vocabulary was built for a model the acceptance path never implemented. The follow-up RQ-030 named is now authorized: remove that machinery rather than leave it. `Production.invalidate_episode_lineage/4` has no reachable caller — accepted lineages form a contiguous prefix and a `request_changes` can only land beyond it, so at the moment of rejection there is by construction nothing downstream to invalidate — and `ensure_not_invalidated/2` runs on every dispatch check while being unable to find anything. A live guard with a dead writer reads as working, and that is worse than a missing guard, so it is deleted rather than kept as reassurance.

## D-0235 — Review happens in the web UI; the generated REVIEW.md workflow is deprecated
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-28
- affects: []
- quote: "we are not to be using review via the review.md workflow. that is long deprecated. all reviews should go via the web ui somehow"
- note: Process discipline. `docs/REVIEW.md` is no longer the author's queue and must not be presented to him as one; agents must stop directing him to read it or to act from it. The review surface is the application. This supersedes the standing line in `AGENTS.md` that "the author reads exactly one file, `docs/REVIEW.md`". The generated file may survive as a machine artifact — `fantasy propagate index` writes it and the propagation gate reads it — but it is an implementation detail, not a workflow, and the web queue must not depend on it: an item awaits the author because its own source document says so in its frontmatter (`status: live`, `awaiting: author`, `ask:`), and the application should read those documents directly rather than a regenerated projection of them. That removes a middleman that has already cost real reliability — the queue's release-SHA binding, its generated-marker check, its row-count reconciliation and its digest staleness all exist only because the projection had to be proved faithful to the sources it was derived from. Rulings recorded in the browser already append the ledger, resolve the source document, and regenerate the indexes; what changes is where the queue comes from and where the author is told to look.

## D-0236 — Engineering design proposals are not the author's queue; agents decide them
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-28
- affects: []
- quote: "also, this \"Canon ruling DP-009-outline-bundle-signoff Approve the fat-bundle sign-off phase between outlining and drafting, so every field the gates demand is settled and signed before expensive writing begins?\" doesnt belong in my review queue"
- note: Process discipline, and the second time the author has said it — D-0232 was "i have no idea. you do it. this doesn't belong in the review queue" about an engineering privilege question. The author's queue carries creative and canon decisions: what is true in the world, what a name is, which text is ratified, whether an episode is acceptable. It does not carry engineering design. A `design-proposal` under `docs/proposals/` describes how the factory should work, and agents decide those; DP-009's fat-bundle sign-off phase is a pipeline design, not a fact about the Hedgeway. Such a document must not set `awaiting: author`, and the queue must not list it. Where a design proposal genuinely contains a creative or canon fork, that fork is extracted and filed as its own `RQ` in the author's own terms — the proposal is not put in front of him wholesale so he can find the one question inside it. This also corrects a fix made earlier the same day: DP-009 was listed with no control, and the repair was to make proposals rulable so the author could act on the item. That answered the wrong question. The item was not un-actionable because a control was missing; it was in a queue it did not belong in, and adding a control made it look legitimate. `AGENTS.md` says an item in the author's queue must be actionable there — the corollary, now explicit, is that anything not his to decide must not be in it.

## D-0238 — A cold-reader revise must commission a revision, not strand the episode
- status: ratified
- date: 2026-07-28
- affects: []
- quote: "Keep blocking, but auto-revise"
- note: The author chose from three presented options after four of an arc's twelve episodes were left unreviewable. A cold-reader verdict of `revise` continues to cap an episode at `candidate` and keep it out of his review queue — he does not want to read work a machine has already judged weak. What changes is that the factory must then COMMISSION the revision rather than leaving the episode stranded, which is what happened on 2026-07-28: episodes 7, 10 and 12 received no second pass at all, and episode 8's remediation budget ran out after a `warn` became a `revise`. Because an arc review packet requires all twelve selections acceptance-ready, four stranded episodes made `/review/arcs/…` return 404 and the whole arc unreviewable. Measured cost is roughly $1.50 per revised episode, which the author accepted as the price of only ever seeing work that passed. Note what this ruling does NOT change: a `warn` verdict does not cap an episode and never did — six episodes of that arc carry a cold-reader `warn` and were promoted to `script` normally, so no relaxation there was needed or made. Separately and not covered by this ruling, episode 11 was capped by a hard `content-integrity` gate that is not one of the reported dimensions: `blocking_gates` was empty, every dimension read `pass`, and the only trace was `worst_status: fail` with a blocking flag whose entire summary was the string "hard gate failed". That invisibility is a defect to fix, not a policy to rule on.
